newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ immigration to be held at current level for now.
newsitem.headline: NZ immigration to be held at current level for now.

text.p: New Zealand's new coalition government said on Wednesday it would hold immigration at current levels for now.

Minority coalition partner New Zealand First has advocated lower immigration. Party leader Winston Peters, a Maori and now Deputy Prime Minister elect, campaigned hard before the October 12 election against high immigration, particularly from Asia.

In a policy agreement signed by NZ First and senior partner, the National Party, it was agreed immigration would reflect New Zealand's needs in terms of skills and ability of the community to absorb migration.
It would also recognise the "diversity of the current New Zealand population".
A population conference would be held in May 1997.
It was agreed to to introduce a four year probationary period for immigrants, health screening and a "clampdown on refugee scams".
